metric_rationale: This metric isolates trials where Option A wins on a strict majority of features (3 out of 4) but Option B wins on the single most valid feature by a large margin (trials 1, 4, 6, 8). Tallying ignores feature validities and magnitudes, simply counting the wins (3 vs 1), and therefore strongly prefers Option A (response = 0). WADD, on the other hand, integrates the large magnitude advantage on the highest-validity cue, allowing it to compensate for the three smaller losses, and thus leans towards Option B (response = 1). The metric computes the mean response on these specific trials, predicting a value close to 0 for Tallying and significantly higher for WADD.

This metric isolates the four specific trial types where the Weighted Additive (WADD) model and the Tallying heuristic make strictly opposing predictions. Tallying relies purely on the count of winning features, ignoring the magnitude of those wins, while WADD computes the validity-weighted sums of the cardinal values. On these filtered trials, Tallying strongly prefers one option due to a 3-to-1 feature win advantage, whereas WADD prefers the opposite option because the single feature loss is overwhelmingly large in magnitude and on the highest validity cue. The metric calculates the proportion of choices on these trials that align with the WADD prediction. A value close to 1 indicates behavior consistent with WADD, while a value close to 0 indicates behavior consistent with Tallying.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic, specifically isolating trials where Tallying makes a strict prediction (i.e., one option wins on more features than the other). On trials 1 and 2 of this design, Tallying and WADD make diametrically opposed predictions because Tallying favors the option with numerous small wins, whereas WADD favors the option with a single massive win on the most valid feature. On trials 5 and 6, Tallying again makes a strict prediction while WADD evaluates them as roughly equal (depending on subjective weights). Therefore, data generated by the Tallying model will yield values close to 1.0 (minus lapse rate), while data generated by WADD will yield much lower values (around 0.25 on average), strongly discriminating the two theories.

In Trial 1, Tallying prefers Option A because it wins on more features (3 vs 2), whereas WADD prefers Option B because B has a massive advantage on the most important features. In Trial 2, Tallying prefers Option B (it wins on 4 out of 5 features), whereas WADD strongly prefers Option A due to a massive advantage on the highest-validity feature. The metric computes the difference in the probability of choosing Option A between Trial 1 and Trial 2. This difference is strongly positive for Tallying and strongly negative for WADD.

This metric computes the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the deterministic prediction of the Take The Best (TTB) heuristic. Because the experimental design explicitly pits TTB against WADD by creating trials where the first discriminating cue favors one option while the remaining cues strongly favor the other, TTB and WADD will systematically predict opposite choices on 5 out of the 6 trial types. Consequently, data simulated under TTB will yield a match rate > 0.5 (albeit noisy due to parameter ranges), whereas data simulated under WADD will yield a match rate significantly below 0.5. This produces a stark and reliable contrast between the two models.

The experimental design pits Take The Best (TTB) against Weighted Additive (WADD) by creating trials where the highest-validity discriminating feature points to one option, but the sum of the remaining lower-validity features strongly favors the other option. This metric dynamically computes the TTB prediction for each trial (by finding the first feature in validity-sorted order that discriminates between the two options) and calculates the proportion of subject responses that align with this prediction. TTB simulated data will yield values significantly above 0.5, whereas WADD simulated data will yield values significantly below 0.5, maximizing the contrast.
